(1) signal activity strongly affects the effective load capacitances and propagation delays of CMOS logic gates, and (2) the peak noise voltage on quiet interconnections can be reduced by increasing the effective output conductances of quiet logic gates driving the interconnect.

the uncertainty in the delay due to the difference in the load capacitance of the logic gates driving the coupled interconnections can exceed 45% and the peak noise voltage on the quiet interconnection can exceed 4%, if the logic gates driving coupled on-chip interconnections are not properly sized.

signal activity has a significant effect on the effective output capacitance of the CMOS logic gates, and that this capacitance should be considered in the sizing of the gates to ensure that they operate properly.

the effect of coupling capacitances between neighboring CMOS logic gate driving coupled interconnections on signal activity.
the effect of interconnect capacitances on CMOS logic gate propagation delay and the noise voltage on coupled interconnections.
the effect of interconnect capacitances on the delay of CMOS logic gates.

the effect of interconnect capacitance coupling on neighboring CMOS gates is a function of the signal activity.

the effect of signal activity on the delay and the peak noise voltage on an interconnection is very significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effective load capacitances of CMOS logic gates are strongly dependent on the signal activity.
the signal activity of neighboring CMOS logic gate outputs should be considered when determining the load capacitance of the quiet gate.
the signal activity has a significant effect on the delay of CMOS logic gates and on the noise induced on quiet interconnections.

the effective output load capacitances of the logic gates should be balanced and the effective output conductances of the logic gate should be increased to minimize the delay and peak noise voltage on quiet interconnections.
